turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Right, Arthur, arm out for me. Blood pressure's 146 over 82, pulse 68, sats 98 percent. Scales are playing up, so we'll skip the weight.
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Ta for that. Parking was a shocker, we did two laps of the block.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm fine. I don't know why she's brought me.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Before you go in, the chemist list has atorvastatin 20 milligrams at night. Is that still what he takes?
[SEG0005] person_2 (CAREGIVER): No, that's old. They put him up to 40 at night for his cholesterol. I pack the Webster pack, so I know it's 40.
[SEG0006] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. She does all that.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): I'll leave it with the doctor. She's free now.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Morning. Have a seat. What's going on?

[SEG0009] person_2 (CAREGIVER): His memory. He asks the same thing over and over, every five minutes, keys, bills, whatever. He's missed two appointments, the dentist and the podiatrist. And last Thursday he got lost between Coles and home.
[SEG0010] person_3 (PATIENT): I didn't get lost. I just took the long way home. And I don't repeat myself.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this been going on?
[SEG0012] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Since Easter. So, six months. Well, actually, about six months.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): No. A few weeks. If that. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any falls?
[SEG0015] person_2 (CAREGIVER): No. None.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Shortness of breath?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Headaches?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Um. No.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): And sleep?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Not great. I wake up a lot. Lie there. I don't know.
[SEG0022] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He's tired of an afternoon as well. Nods off in the recliner, mid-sentence sometimes.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Medicines. You manage them?

[SEG0024] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Yes. Perindopril 5 milligrams in the morning for the blood pressure. Atorvastatin at night for the cholesterol, 40, like I told the nurse, not 20. And a little white tablet for his stomach. Name's gone. Every time.
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): I stopped the sleeping tablet in March. The temazepam. Made me foggy.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): What strength?
[SEG0027] person_2 (CAREGIVER): 10 milligrams, at night. He only took it for a bit, then stopped it himself in March. Hasn't had it since.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah. I don't know the number.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Was he given aspirin?
[SEG0030] person_2 (CAREGIVER): He was, and he never took it. Not once. I didn't even pop the foil. Reckoned it was for old people, he did.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does the pack actually get taken every day?
[SEG0032] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Mostly. When I'm at bowls on a Tuesday I'm not sure about the morning ones. I've come home and they're still sitting in the pack.
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): I do take them. Well. I think I do. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0035] person_2 (CAREGIVER): No. No allergies.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): I don't think so.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Blood pressure and cholesterol, longstanding?
[SEG0038] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Blood pressure for about ten years. Cholesterol came along after. Both still going.
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Operations?
[SEG0040] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Cataracts, both eyes, about four years back. Nothing else.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0042] person_3 (PATIENT): Gave it up. Years back. Used to be rollies.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0044] person_3 (PATIENT): A beer with dinner. Most nights. That's all.
[SEG0045] person_2 (CAREGIVER): It's just us two at home. He's retired. Fitter and turner, he was, at the council depot.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Memory problems in the family?
[SEG0047] person_2 (CAREGIVER): His mum had dementia. She was in a home by the end. His dad went with his heart, but that's not today's issue.
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): Where are we, right now?
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): The clinic. I think. Your rooms.
[SEG0050] person_4 (DOCTOR): What day is it?
[SEG0051] person_3 (PATIENT): Tuesday? Um. I don't know.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): It's Thursday. On your feet a second. Gait's steady. No tremor.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'm not putting a label on this today. Could be a memory disorder, could be the tablets, could be a low B12. I am not calling it dementia. Let's see what the tests say.
[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll organise bloods, B12 and thyroid included, and I'll book a memory assessment.
[SEG0055] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Do you want a scan? My sister won't shut up about scans.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): We might do a head CT if the bloods don't explain it. I'm not ordering one today.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): No walking to the shops on your own for now. And keep a note of the questions he repeats, roughly when.
[SEG0058] person_4 (DOCTOR): See me in six weeks with the results. if he gets lost again, or if there's a fall, come back sooner.
[SEG0059] person_3 (PATIENT): Six weeks. Alright. I still reckon I'm fine.
[SEG0060] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Thanks. Come on, the parking meter's not going to wait.

spec.situation: Spouse brings an older person who 'is fine' but repeats questions, forgets appointments and got lost; patient disagrees on many points; medicines managed by spouse; doctor plans bloods and a memory assessment, no diagnosis said aloud.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.

bad.reason: Transcript says 'just us two at home' but does not state spouse explicitly.
bad.text: living (description=Lives with his spouse, just the two of them, status=current, reported_by=caregiver)

bad.text: Temazepam (generic_name=temazepam, dose=10 mg, frequency=at night, indication=sleep, status=discontinued, reported_by=caregiver)

bad.text: Knows he is in the clinic (status=present, observed_by=doctor)

bad.reason: Patient answers 'Tuesday' and doctor corrects to Thursday; not directly observed-only from questioning.
Doctor told caregiver/pair to keep notes; responsible person not specifically the patient.
bad.text: Keep a note of repeated questions and roughly when they happen (action_type=counselling, status=recommended, responsible_person=patient)

omissions.text: Atorvastatin current dose is 40 mg at night, not 20 mg; the recorded medication entry is missing the dose.
Temazepam 10 mg at night was stopped by the patient himself in March because it made him foggy; the adverse effect/reason for stopping is not recorded.
Aspirin had been prescribed previously but he never took it, not once.
Medication adherence detail: the Webster pack is taken only 'mostly'; on Tuesdays when the caregiver is at bowls, the morning tablets are sometimes left in the pack.
Sleep symptom detail: patient says sleep is 'not great.'
No weight was obtained because the scales were not working.

Orientation finding was uncertain/incomplete: when asked where they were, the patient answered 'The clinic. I think. Your rooms.' rather than clearly demonstrating orientation; recording this simply as 'Knows he is in the clinic' overstates the finding.
Doctor explicitly said he is not calling this dementia today.
